A1.justification: Both complete 54-page PDFs describe PANGEA, PANGEAIns and PANGEABench. Their main text, tables, figures and appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations in Tables 2–3 and Appendix I, training-data analyses in Figures 5–7, and multilingual OCR experiments in Appendix J.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark evaluations, training-data analyses and multilingual OCR experiments.

M1.justification: The LLaVA-Next architecture, Qwen2-7B-Instruct backbone, CLIP vision encoder, two-stage training and instruction-construction pipeline remain unchanged. Section 2.2 reorganizes the explanation of recaptioning and instruction generation without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training languages, 14-dataset evaluation suite and supplementary OCR coverage. The corrected Hebrew illustration in Figure 25 does not establish expanded coverage: Hebrew already appears in both versions' language inventory.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding main and appendix comparisons. Tables 2–3 retain the same proprietary, English-centric, multilingual and text-only baseline rows.

E3.justification: Training configurations, benchmark subsets, metrics and evaluation procedures remain unchanged, including the xChat judging protocol in Appendix E and OCR experiment in Appendix J. Rewritten descriptions do not document revised settings.

E4.justification: The instruction-count, English-data proportion and language-distribution analyses remain unchanged, as do the xChat success/failure examples and OCR pilot. The qualitative chat discussion moves from Section 5 to Appendix F rather than introducing a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or statistical testing procedures. The reporting practices in the retained tables and plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: The introduction changes the reported gains from 0.4 and 10.9 points to 0.4% and 10.9%. Table 2 still reports 59.9 versus 59.5 for English and 52.8 versus 41.9 for multilingual averages in both versions. This changes the stated margin units, not measured performance; the benchmark and analysis results otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised. The existing xChat score normalization and mathematical material in examples are unchanged.

C1.justification: The headline quantitative comparison is recast from point differences to percentages, introducing ambiguity about the claimed improvement. The central contributions and claims of multilingual and multicultural performance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 removes the explicit rationale that native-language captions add authenticity and help models learn language-specific nuances. Other substantive interpretations and limitations remain, including the chat failure discussion relocated to Appendix F and OCR limitations retained in Appendix J.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page URL on the title page, providing an additional access pointer for the work. Existing training configurations, hardware/time information, construction prompts and evaluation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a change in external resource availability.

R1.justification: The reference list contains the same works, and the research positioning remains unchanged. Appendix A changes citation punctuation and formatting without adding prior work or revising comparisons.

P1.justification: v3 tightens prose across the introduction, dataset construction, benchmark descriptions and discussion. It reorganizes Section 2.2, moves existing qualitative discussion to Appendix F, adds acknowledgments and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR publication header.

P2.justification: Figure 25 replaces a duplicated Tamil example incorrectly captioned as Hebrew with a Hebrew example about Jerusalem. Figure 2's caption is shortened, and existing tables, plots and qualitative material are repositioned as the document reflows.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 25's mismatched illustration, clarifying the data-generation narrative and adding a project-page link modestly improve accuracy and usability. The empirical evidence is unchanged. These gains are limited by the less precise percentage wording for point differences and a new Section 5 reference to Appendix E where the qualitative discussion is actually in Appendix F.
